transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… honestly, it’s gotten embarrassing. I clean buildings for work, and lately the thought of seeing a rat has gotten so bad that I’m having trouble doing parts of my job. Like if I know I have to go into a trash room, or an older part of a building, I just freeze up or avoid it, even if I’m telling myself, “It’s probably fine, it’s just an old building, it’s not actually dangerous.” 

But my mind just goes straight to, what if there’s a rat in there, what if I see one, what if it runs near me. And I know that sounds like a small thing, maybe, but it’s really starting to interfere with what I’m supposed to do every day.

When you think about going into places where you might see a rat, or when you actually see one, does your anxiety get so intense that you experience physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shaking?

Yes. It comes on really fast, like before I even have a chance to talk myself down. If I’m walking toward a trash room or near the back hallway and I hear something like scratching in the wall, or I see just a little movement near a pipe or along the floor, my whole body reacts right away.

My heart starts pounding hard, my hands shake, and I feel like I have to get out of there immediately. It’s not like I calmly think, “Oh, that might be a rat.” It’s more like my body decides for me, and then my brain catches up after. I can be standing there with cleaning supplies in my hand, knowing I’m supposed to keep working, and I just… I can’t think straight for a minute. I’m only focused on getting away from that spot.
